top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a simple, well-understood mechanism (the magic wavelength cancels the lattice light shift) that has been checked systematically and reproduced by independent clocks agreeing near 1e-18. The two-name allocation to Katori (proposal and first demonstration) and Ye (accuracy and many-body regime) is clean, and a citation tied to the magic-wavelength lattice clock separates it from the earlier frequency-comb and ion-control prizes. This is better than no award, though KPZ remains my scientifically most universal candidate and is not on the slate.
